top_choice_rationale: P001 (Helpman and Grossman, with the citation confined to the political economy of trade protection) is the strongest proposal on achievement, maturity, attribution and citation scope. The protection-for-sale framework turned lobbying and tariff formation into a tractable equilibrium object with sharp cross-sector predictions, and about thirty years of theory, testing and trade-agreement analysis have built on it. Credit sits cleanly with a two-person joint programme, with no co-originator at the same level left out. The main reservation is the mixed, specification-sensitive empirical record. That makes this an organising framework and research agenda, not a confirmed quantitative result, and the citation should not claim validation. I weigh that as a real limit but not a disqualifying one. P002 (Autor, Dorn, Hanson) is now a stable three-name set with a narrowed citation and strong design-based evidence. I rank it second because the long-run magnitudes and shift-share identification are still being revised and the task-framework antecedents are not credited. P003 (Melitz, Helpman) is an important and densely tested contribution, but the exporter facts and parallel models of Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum cannot be credited within the set. No award is last, because P001 to P003 are each substantive, mature contributions. This ranking rests on the written round-2 arguments and my own judgement, not on the number of supporters, and I have not independently verified any claim about the 2008 or 2025 prizes.
recusal_note: No connection to Helpman, Grossman, Autor, Dorn, Hanson, Melitz or any other credited name is apparent from my profile. I have co-authored with committee chair John Hassler and former chair Tore Ellingsen (IJIO 2026). My profile lists no co-authorship with a credited name on P001, P002 or P003. My field is industrial organisation and international trade, so I may know P001 and P003 more closely than other fields. I am married to Magdalena Andersson, a former Swedish prime minister, which is noted only as a public fact and has no apparent bearing on any candidate. Disclosed, not adjudicated.
